title: Research 2/9: the ratio identification problem - author-declared vs successor-extracted ratio decidendi
description: Research agenda item 2 (docs/civilizational-roadmap-brief.md:50). Extracting the ratio decidendi from a judgment is itself a contested interpretive act - later courts partly decide what an earlier case stood for. Research how that ambiguity is managed in practice (at minimum: the Wambaugh inversion test, Goodhart's material-facts approach, narrow vs wide ratio, the role of headnotes and official reporters, and how later courts reformulate a holding). Then decide whether this harness resolves it STRUCTURALLY (the author declares the ratio at write time) or INTERPRETIVELY (successors extract it), and cost each choice. Output docs/precedent-research/02-ratio-identification.md. Web research, tagged claims, mandatory implications section.

This verdict is consumed directly by T-339.

MUST engage this measured corpus finding and let it shape the recommendation: an agent's self-declared BENEFIT attribution is roughly trustworthy (precision 33.7% / recall 51.4%, about 5x random) while its self-predicted SCOPE OF HARM is not (regression precision 11.8% / recall 11.1%, about 2x the 5.6%/5.4% random baselines) - papers/agentic_harness_engineering.pdf:9, section 4.4.2 'Regression blindness'. Recommend explicitly which record fields may be AUTHOR-DECLARED and bind on publication, and which must be VERIFIER-CONFIRMED before they bind.

MUST propose the concrete field split for the PR record: what the author writes (ratio), what is explicitly non-binding (dicta), and what is written by the author but marked unconfirmed until a verifier confirms it (scope conditions / blast radius). Name the field names you recommend.
MUST address the failure mode where an author declares an artificially WIDE ratio to bind successors beyond what the work supports, and name a detectable signal for it.
